item.title: Netanyahu condemns Binyamin riots: 'Prosecute the rioters to the fullest extent of the law'
item.description:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned on Tuesday morning the violent riots that took place overnight in the Binyamin region and the attacks on security forces who arrived at the scene.
"The handful of rioters does not represent the law-abiding settler population in Judea and Samaria; it does a tremendous injustice and interferes with our forces in carrying out their mission," Netanyahu said.
Netanyahu expressed his support for the IDF soldiers and Border Police officers operating in the area and called on law enforcement authorities to take action against those involved.
"I fully support the IDF soldiers and Border Police officers who are working to thwart terrorism and maintain security, and I call on law enforcement authorities to prosecute the rioters to the fullest extent of the law," he stated.

item.title: Herzog on Samaria riot: 'A moral stain and an affront to the rule of law'
item.description:
President Isaac Herzog condemned the violence in the village of Jalud, calling it "an extremely serious incident that must be dealt with to the fullest extent of the law. It is a moral stain and an affront to the rule of law."
"Arson, rock-throwing, and the assault and injury of IDF soldiers and Border Police officers are absolutely prohibited and can have no justification whatsoever," he said.
Herzog called on the authorities "to act decisively against the lawbreakers and bring them to justice."

item.title: Minister Sa'ar condemns Samaria riot: Rioters 'harm our values, Jewish settlement, and Israel'
item.description:
Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar condemned the overnight riots in the area of the village of Jalud in Samaria, which included the torching of property and injuries to Border Police officers. Sa'ar stated that an investigation had been launched and called for it to be conducted thoroughly and comprehensively to bring the rioters to justice.
"Those who commit these criminal offenses, divert the attention of Border Police and IDF soldiers, and even harm them, are criminals who must be dealt with to the fullest extent of the law," Sa'ar said. According to him, the rioters "harm our values, Jewish settlement, and Israel."

item.title: Jerusalem: Five arrested at celebration following disturbances and light rail obstruction
item.description:
Police arrested five suspects during a celebration in Jerusalem on suspicion of disorderly conduct and violence against civilians and police officers.
Among other incidents, a gathering on Haim Bar-Lev and Sachs streets blocked the light rail tracks while trains were being moved. Police used crowd-dispersal measures to restore order at the scene.
